assets.title: The hand out early.
assets.prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: wide landscape lesson panel for a Grade 6–8 Crew SEL learning pack. Side-view illustration of exactly two middle-school runners practicing a relay on a simple outdoor track, both moving toward the right, ample space separating their bodies. Trailing runner on left: a boy with short dark curls, mustard athletic shirt and navy shorts, one foot on track and other leg bent in running stride. His near arm extends forward from his natural shoulder, elbow gently bent, hand holding one short coral relay baton horizontally. His other arm bends back at his side. Leading runner on right: a girl with a neat brown ponytail, teal athletic shirt and navy shorts, mid-stride. Her near arm reaches backward from its own shoulder with a small natural elbow bend; an open hand faces back toward the approaching baton. Her other arm bends forward naturally. Small clear gap between baton and receiving palm, handoff has not occurred yet. Exactly two arms and two legs per runner, shoulders elbows wrists anatomically connected, normal joints, distinct non-overlapping silhouettes, hands on correct wrists, coherent hair connected to heads. Simple parallel curved track lines, no lane numbers. Warm simple flat educational illustration, clean rounded shapes, muted coral, mustard, teal and navy, pale warm cream background, subtle paper texture. Wide landscape composition with whole bodies visible. No text, words, letters, numerals, labels, captions, logos, watermark or extra runners.
assets.caption: waiting with your hands down is how relays get dropped.
